messages.author: 881c51ed14655bd5
messages.subject: Global Options vs. Default parameters.
parts:
Yihui and other knitr users,

I would like to question the use within knitr of global options through opts_chunk and others vs supplying default arguments. and using the global objects as the defaults.  The latest issue that I came across with the render_gfm() being required to be called from within the document highlights this problem.  I find myself wanting to be able knit several documents in a single session, perhaps two markdown and a sweave in the same setting.

With a language like R that has powerful, albeit sometime confusing lexical scope issues, care needs to be taken with global objects.  I think that there might be merit in considering a scheme were we can make inferences with reasonable defaults but avoid the issues that are coming from the global object use.

This may also help remedy the situation of the _knit_ naming convention, since the format could be specified on the command line.

Thanks,
Andrew

then the output hooks will be global to this R session. I ought to be
able not to override users' pre-defined hooks, and I think I can do it
in v0.4.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: Global Options vs. Default parameters.
parts:
Hi Andrew,

Things should be cleaner now in the current development version. You
can call render_gfm() before knit(), and knitr will no longer override
your hooks. They work through the whole R session unless you change
them explicitly later. Now the customization is more natural:

pat_xxx() # set pattern list
render_xxx() # set output hooks
knit_hooks$set() # if you still have other hooks
opts_chunk$set() # set chunk options
opts_knit$set() # package options
knit() # ready to knit

All these changes before knit() are permanent in an R session.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Global Options vs. Default parameters.
parts:
Yes, you are free to do it; just think the function render_foobar() as
options(), like

x = rnorm(100)

options(width = 50)
print(x)

options(width = 90)
print(x)
# width will stay as 90 unless you change it later

thus after you have changed the hooks by render_foobar(), you can
knit() a bunch of files to the 'foobar' format without having to call
render_foobar() inside these files.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Global Options vs. Default parameters.
parts:
Perhaps it is just me getting stuck on things, but I think that there
are merits for both approaches.  Thank you for fixing the bug, but it
is a little aside from my original point.  IT might be nice to define
things in both terms of global parameters, that can at any individual
function call be overridden.  Something along the lines of the
following

````r
#define knit
knit = function(input, output = NULL, tangle = FALSE, text = NULL,
chuck = opts_chunk$get(), knit = opts_knit$get(), hooks =
knit_hooks$get, patterns = knit_patterns$get()
){
. . .
}
````
then for any call scope stays local to the function, but defaults to
global defaults. That would enable something like
```r
knit("in.md", "out.md", chunk= within(opts_chunk$get(), {cache=T}))
```
Would you be open to some structure along those lines?

-Andrew

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Global Options vs. Default parameters.
parts:
I think I understand what you mean, but as we discussed in
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/19 a few months ago, I tend to
keep the number of arguments of a function minimal. On one hand, this
is like ggplot2 vs base R graphics/lattice: you can draw a plot in a
huge function call, or you do your job in small pieces; the procedure
below is the workflow to knit() a document:

pat_xxx() # set pattern list
render_xxx() # set output hooks
knit_hooks$set() # if you still have other hooks
opts_chunk$set() # set chunk options
opts_knit$set() # package options
knit() # ready to knit

They are global changes (in terms of the current R session). If you
want to tweak a small number of options inside your document, you can
use \SweaveOpts{} -- this is the second global level (global in terms
of this document, and will be restored when you exit this document).
Then you still have local options in <<>>=; this is the lowest level
-- these options only affect this chunk. I'm not sure if I made these
three levels clear.

On the other hand, I'm kind of pushing users to the reproducible end:
ideally all the above settings can be done inside a document except
pat_xxx(), i.e. make the document as self-contained as possible. But
this will obviously annoy users since it would require them to repeat
the settings in all documents, so there comes the above highest global
settings.

I'm wondering how frequently you need to change all these options, and
why "setting (a large number of) global options outside + (a small
number of) local options inside" is difficult for you.

BTW, I almost always call knitr via Rscript to avoid option/object
clashes, and I group similar types of documents and compile them
together, so I do not need to change all these options/hooks
frequently.

Regards,
Yihui
